hooks.text: The Nazca carved giant lines by clearing the trees holding their desert.
How did cutting down trees destroy a brilliant desert civilization?
Ancient desert geoglyphs were preserved by the very trees that destroyed their creators.

title: Why Did the Nazca Civilization Cut Down Its Own Desert? 🗿
description: Discover the tragic mystery of the Nazca civilization, whose reliance on agriculture and clearing of native trees led to their sudden collapse after ancient floods.

beats.text: Intricate geoglyphs of animals stretched across more than 1,300 kilometers of dry plateau.

beats.text: Expanding maize and cotton agriculture required removing deep-rooted Huarango trees.
beats.visual: The Huarango tree in the Peruvian desert, photograph, 2018

beats.text: An El Niño event around 500 AD unleashed torrential coastal flooding.
beats.visual: Southern Peru topography map, cartographic image, 2010

beats.text: Without root systems, the unprotected soil washed away into deep river channels.
beats.visual: Entrance to a Nazca underground aqueduct or puquio, photograph, 2012

beats.text: Their sophisticated irrigation aqueducts dried up as the civilization collapsed into a barren desert.
